Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1234 PM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER MUCH OF
CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA...AND FROM EASTERN IOWA INTO NORTHERN
INDIANA...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered damaging winds may occur Sunday from eastern Iowa across
northern Illinois and Indiana. A concentrated area of damaging wind
and hail is also expected over much of South Dakota.

...From eastern IA into northern IN...
Storms, possibly producing strong wind gusts, may be ongoing over
much of the area Sunday morning. This potentially severe activity
could persist for much of the day as it travels southeastward with
access to a destabilizing air mass.

Behind the early activity, strong instability will develop as
low-level winds remain out of the southwest. While mid to upper
level winds will not be particularly strong, the veering low-level
winds and likelihood of redevelopment along any outflow boundaries
suggests additional severe storms during the late afternoon, moving
across much of the same areas as the early day storms. Damaging
winds appear to be the primary concern, however, a brief tornado
cannot be ruled out early in the redevelopment cycle as low-level
instability will be large, with perhaps enhanced low-level shear
near residual outflows.

...Dakotas...
Moderate northwest flow aloft will persist over the region, with
surface winds veering to east/southeast late in the day. A moist
plume should be maintained over SD within the recovering warm
advection regime, with evening 850 mb winds also increasing out of
the south. Surface based storms are expected to develop into much of
SD, with an initial large hail threat. With time, an MCS could
develop, producing a swath of damaging winds. Isolated significant
wind gusts cannot be ruled out.

..Southern AZ...
Easterly flow aloft around the upper high will support a westward
component to the storms motions on Sunday, possibly bringing locally
strong gusts into the lower elevations as storms move out of Mexico,
and possibly off the Rim. Substantial PWAT will remain over the
region with 60s F dewpoints which when combined with steep low-level
lapse rates will support afternoon storms and locally severe gusts.

...Southern Appalachians...
Storms will form over the higher terrain Sunday afternoon from
northern GA into the western Carolinas. Given sufficient storm
concentration, a few damaging gusts cannot be ruled out as storms
and outflows generally spread eastward into the diurnally heating
air mass.

..Jewell.. 08/08/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0231 PM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM ILLINOIS
EASTWARD INTO PENNSYLVANIA...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible on Monday from
northern Illinois eastward into western Pennsylvania. Isolated
severe gusts and hail will also be possible from parts of the
central and northern Plains into the Midwest.

...Midwest / OH Valley / Mid Atlantic...
An elongated zone of damaging wind potential will exist on Monday
from Illinois to the Mid Atlantic, with various clusters of storms
throughout the period.

Earlier in the day, it appears ongoing activity may be present
around OH, with moderate 40+ kt midlevel westerlies pushing the
activity toward the Mid Atlantic during the afternoon. There, it
could encounter the destabilizing air mass, with possible new
development and/or rejuvenation with damaging gust potential.

Farther west, a large area of strong instability is forecast across
the Midwest, with an east-west oriented boundary roughly from IA
across northern IL/IN/OH. Parts of this boundary may be
re-positioned depending on the extent of early day outflows.

West to southwest 850 mb winds over 30 kt should help maintain
low-level moisture/heat flux into the frontal zone, with new
development most likely across the Slight Risk area from northern IL
into OH. Corridors of damaging winds will be possible with the
resulting clusters or MCS, possibly affecting northern KY into WV.
Predictability remains fairly low or this pattern.

...Northern Plains...
Low pressure is forecast to develop over the central Plain, while
moisture and backed surface winds persist generally north of I-80.
Strong heating and surface convergence should support afternoon
development over western SD, and perhaps elevated storms later over
ND. Isolated severe gusts or hail will be possible over SD and
vicinity, perhaps into northern NE and western IA overnight. A
targeted Slight Risk may be needed in later updates as
predictability increases.

..Jewell.. 08/08/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0355 AM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

Valid 111200Z - 161200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Tuesday/Day 4 and Wednesday/Day 5...
A broad cyclonic mid-level flow pattern is forecast from the upper
Mississippi Valley into the Northeast on Tuesday and Wednesday. At
the surface, a moist airmass is forecast to be in place over most of
the eastern half of the nation with a quasi-stationary front located
from the northern Plains east-southeastward into the southern Great
Lakes. To the south of the front, surface dewpoints in the 70s F
will likely result in the development of moderate to strong
instability. Isolated to scattered thunderstorms appear likely to
develop each afternoon in areas where low-level convergence becomes
maximized. Outflow boundaries will be important in determining where
the greatest convective coverage ends up being. In addition to the
instability, moderate deep-layer shear is forecast over much of this
moist airmass suggesting that an isolated wind-damage threat will be
possible. However, the lack of any appreciable mid-level shortwave
trough introduces considerable uncertainty.

...Thursday/Day 6 and Saturday/Day 8...
From Thursday to Saturday, mid-level flow is forecast to become
westerly over much of the northern U.S, with a front located from
the central Plains eastward into the southern Great Lakes and Ohio
Valley. Thunderstorm development will be possible each afternoon and
evening near this front. Surface dewpoints in the 70s F to the south
of the front, along with moderate to strong instability will make
isolated severe thunderstorms possible each afternoon and evening.
However, spatial uncertainty concerning any potential severe threat
is considerable at this range.

..Broyles.. 08/08/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1215 AM CDT Sun Aug 09 2026

Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE MIDWEST...AND PORTIONS OF THE DAKOTAS...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered damaging winds may occur today into this evening from
southern Minnesota and eastern Iowa eastward across parts of
northern Illinois, southern Wisconsin, southern Lower Michigan,
northwest Ohio, and northern Indiana. Damaging wind and hail is also
expected across portions of the Dakotas.

...IA/MN into the Midwest...

Convection is expected to be ongoing this morning across parts of
southern MN into eastern IA. This early day activity could pose a
risk for damaging gusts. This activity is likely to continue to
spread eastward across the Lake Michigan vicinity through the
afternoon on the nose a of modest low-level jet and along a surface
front oriented across southern WI and Lower MI. This activity could
intensify as is moves into a destabilizing airmass by midday. 

Additional development is possible within the moisture rich warm
sector across northern IL/IN along the southern flank of ongoing
convection and/or outflow. Strong to extreme instability is
forecast, while vertically veering wind profiles support 30+ kt
effective shear magnitudes. Low-level SRH also will be enhanced
along the surface boundary. While damaging winds are expected to be
the primary hazard with convection, some risk for hail and a tornado
or two also will exist through evening. Depending on the evolution
of morning convection, it is possible higher probabilities will be
needed in subsequent outlooks.

...Dakotas and western NE...

A surface front is expected to develop southward across the central
Plains, becoming oriented across northern KS by tonight. Low-level
warm advection atop the boundary, and surface winds becoming
south/southeasterly with time will maintain 60s dewpoints across the
region. Within this post-frontal upslope regime, moderate
northwesterly flow aloft will persist. A modest south/southwesterly
low-level jet is also forecast to develop during the evening hours.
Low-level convergence within the warm advection regime and
increasing low-level jet may be sufficient for isolated to scattered
thunderstorm development. Supercell wind profiles and steep
low-level lapse rates will support initial storms capable of large
hail and damaging winds. If sufficient clusters/outflow
consolidation can occur, upscale growth during the late evening into
overnight hours is possible, with an increasing risk for swaths of
severe/damaging gusts.

...Southern Appalachians...

Scattered thunderstorm development is expected over higher terrain
within a seasonally moist and unstable airmass. Steepening low-level
lapse rates and high PW values may support locally strong gusts with
wet microbursts through early evening.

...AZ...

Modest easterly mid/upper flow will persist across the region on the
southern periphery of an upper high over the Four Corners. Another
day of hot conditions will promote steep lapse rates and modest
destabilization. As convection develops over higher terrain and
spread westward, strong outflow gusts may occur.

..Leitman/Moore.. 08/09/2026
